spec: 10 §6 (identifiers: OrderKey as generation id, CancelOp, FillKey), 10 S4, 12 §7.1 (cid -> current OrderKey; late events for older generations), 12 §7.3 (CancelOrder binding per profile), 13 §5.1 Cancels (TC-C5), 13 §5.4 (unbound delayed cancel TS bug), 30 §5.2 (order(), orders()), 60 §5.10 (cid generations), src/trading/cancellation.test.ts:768-958 (cited scenarios)
notes: A reused cid gets a new OrderKey; cid -> current key points at the latest submission; earlier keys stay in the ledger; a late event for an older generation updates only that generation's record (12 §7.1).

OrderKeys are dense from 0 per session, assigned in intent-processing order to SUBMISSIONS (orders that reach OrderSubmitted). Engine-origin rejections carry no key (12 §9.2: OM-level rejections do not touch the ledger).

The cited TS tests use GTC BUY UP 10 @ 0.5 with cid buy-up, a book with best bid 0.4 / best ask 0.6, and a later tick with best ask 0.4 (strictly below the limit) to produce a maker fill of the whole order under WorstQueueCompat.

Observability of OrderKey from strategy code: the spec renders the simulator exchange id as sim-{order_key} at I/O (10 §6) but 10 §10.1 marks OrderAccepted.exchange_id as `(live)`; whether backtests expose it is PLAN.md ambiguity A-14. The tests below assert through portfolio views and traces where possible.
